1282. 1. September. ProtiWins. — Die Brüder Leutold, Ulrich und Rueger, genannt Prneschinchen, schenken dem Ctstercienserstifte Hohenfurt einen JUansus in Einsiedl.

XXXI. Quoniam deprecado justi assidua etdeuociomultum valent felix- que memoria summum bonum: nos igitur Levtoldus Vlricus et Rue- gerus fratres dicti Prueschinchen venerabilis abbatis nee non tocius conuentus Altouadensis ecclesie Cysterciensis ordinis sanete deuo, cioni inuolui cupientes felicique memorie nos humiliter committentes notum esse volumus vniuersis, quibus exhibitum fuerit presens scriptum, quod eidem ecclesie predicte in Altouado mansum situm in Nevzadling cum omnibus suis redditibus et vsibus pretaxatis, soluen- tibus annuatim videlicet VI metretis siliginis vno modio auene VI solidis denariorum Wiennensium siue porco talento etiam pro steura nee non aliis minutis seruiciis, a nobis ibidem super altare glorio- sissime Marie virginis iuste et racionabiliter delegatum concedimus et donamus perpetuo possidendum. Vt autem hec donaciopermaneat inconuulsa et rata omnimodis teneatur presentes sibi literas cum aр- pensione nostri sigilli dedimus et munimine roboratas. Testibus etiam subnotatis: Domino Wernhardo de Schaumberch seniore nee non fratre eius domino Hainrico filiisque eorum Hainrico seniore et Wernhardo juniore; domino Hainrico de Rosenberch, domino Jo hanne venerabile plebano in Netolicz, domino Vrso capellano nee non Rudolfo notario Prueschinchorum. et aliis quam pluribus fide dignis. Datum anno domini M°C°C°lxxxii. in Protiwins in die sancti Egidii confessoris. Gut erhaltenes, thalergrosses, an Pergamentslreifen hangendes Siegel in weissem Wachs. — Vorderseite: Rundes Siegel; ein Helm mit flügelartigem 37 • Schmuck. — -j- S. Vlrici Prvschinch!. — Rückseite: Dreieckiges Siegel ein durch einen Querbalken getheilter Schild. — S. Levtoldi. Prveschio. 2. Millaucr p. 86, n. 16.
entries.english: We, Leutold, Ulrich, and Rueger, brothers called Prueschinchen, wishing to embrace the holy devotion of the venerable abbot and the whole convent of the Cistercian church at Hohenfurt, humbly commend ourselves to their good memory. We make known that we grant to that church, to possess perpetually, a mansus at Neuzadling with all its revenues and uses, which pay annually six measures of rye, one modius of oats, six Viennese solidi or a pig, a talent for tax, and other minor services. We have justly and reasonably assigned it there upon the altar of the most glorious Virgin Mary. To keep the gift firm and unshaken, we issued this charter confirmed by the appending of our seal. Witnesses: Wernhard von Schaumberg der Ältere and his brother Heinrich, their sons Heinrich der Ältere and Wernhard der Jüngere, Lord Heinrich von Rosenberg, Lord Johannes, venerable parish priest at Netolitz, Lord Ursus the chaplain, Rudolf, notary of the Prueschinken, and many other trustworthy men. Given at Protivins on the feast of Saint Giles, 1 September 1282. The well-preserved, thaler-sized seal of white wax hangs from a parchment strip: on the front is a round seal with a helmet and wing-shaped ornament, inscribed “Seal of Ulrich Pruesching”; the reverse shows a triangular shield divided by a crossbar, inscribed “Seal of Leutold Prueschin.” Reference: Millauer, p. 86, no. 16.
